audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart handed Akali Levels 2, 3, First item and Two+ items and called Level 6 Skill, while every whys[] entry argued the opposite shape.
audit.why: packet.levelChart is Sion / Skill / Skill / Skill / Akali / Skill / Sion, and the existing whys already say Sion owns Level 1 (no shroud yet) and the very late brawl, Akali owns the level-6 burst, and the rest is even.
audit.corrected: Level 1 to Sion, Levels 2 and 3 to Skill, Level 6 to Akali, First item to Skill, Two+ items to Sion. Proposed as matched full/content pairs.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 phase text was boilerplate and never named Perfect Execution or its two-cast structure.
audit.why: Akali R is Perfect Execution, 120/90/60s, 675 range, an execute on the second cast; that is the single spike that decides this lane.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why now names Perfect Execution, its R1/E/R2 sequence, and the condition for fighting at 6 (Soul Furnace up, a charge ready).

audit.whatIsWrong: Text repeatedly claimed Twilight Shroud lets her 'dodge' a charged Q, and claimed Sion's W is a physical-damage reduction. Akali's Q cooldown was given as a 3-second window.
audit.why: Riot text: Twilight Shroud makes her invisible and unselectable — that denies your aim, not a ground-area swing, which is exactly the error the mirror audit fixed on her page. Soul Furnace is a flat shield with a 15s cooldown, not physical reduction. Five Point Strike is on a 1.5s cooldown and gated by Energy, not 3s.
audit.corrected: wants.foe[0] restated as losing sight of her mid-charge; the late-game tail now says the smoke hides her from your aim so you swing where she stood; early names Five Point Strike's magic damage and Soul Furnace's 15s cooldown; mid corrects the Q cooldown to 1.5s energy-gated.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing told you what her commit tell actually is.
audit.why: Assassin's Mark rings a target on spell damage and empowers her next attack when she leaves the ring — the step-out, not the cast, is the burst tell.
audit.corrected: mid now states the Assassin's Mark ring proc is the commit tell, not her cast.

edits.before: At level 1 Akali has no shroud and no escape — she is uniquely vulnerable to a cold-opened fully charged Q that most melee champions would just walk out of. Respect that window: hold behind your wave, bait her forward with apparent passive farming, and release the charge the instant she steps into knockup range. If you land it, E to armor-shred and W-detonate immediately while she is grounded. If you miss, back off — her Q poke is magic damage that bypasses your W-shield's physical reduction, so eating two or three uncontested Qs erodes enough health to flip the trade math by level 3. Your W's detonation on short trades is your equalization tool: she trades one Q proc, you trade a W detonation, and your passive glory-in-death means she never gets free value even if she wins the all-in.
edits.after: At level 1 Akali has no shroud and no escape — she is uniquely vulnerable to a cold-opened fully charged Q that most melee champions would just walk out of. Respect that window: hold behind your wave, bait her forward with apparent passive farming, and release the charge the instant she steps into knockup range. If you land it, Roar of the Slayer to shred armour and detonate Soul Furnace while she is stunned. If you miss, back off — Five Point Strike pokes magic damage and Soul Furnace only answers it every 15s, so two or three uncontested Qs flip the trade math by level 3. The 3-second detonation on short trades is your equalizer: she trades one Q proc, you trade the blast, and your passive means she never gets free value even if she wins the all-in.

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are the flattest stretch — you have your full basic kit but no Unstoppable Onslaught, and Akali has enough Energy regeneration to fish Q pokes on a 3-second window that is shorter than your Q charge time. Do not charge Q in her direct line of sight; use side-brush angles or a minion wall to obscure the glow, then step and release. At level 6 she gets her R and the dynamic flips sharply: R1 closes the gap, her E repositions, and R2 executes you below half. Do not fight her post-6 unless your W-shield is full and you have the stun ready to interrupt between her two R casts — the window between R1 landing and R2 becoming usable is roughly 1.5 seconds, just enough to land a charged Q and deny the execute.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are the flattest stretch — you have your full basic kit but no Unstoppable Onslaught, and Akali can fish Five Point Strike on a 1.5-second cooldown, gated only by Energy. Her Assassin's Mark ring proc is the commit tell, not her cast. Do not charge Q in her line of sight; use brush or a minion wall to hide the glow, then step and release. At level 6 the dynamic flips sharply: R1 closes the gap, her E repositions, and R2 executes you below the threshold. Do not fight her post-6 unless Soul Furnace is up and you have the stun ready to interrupt between her two R casts — that gap is roughly 1.5 seconds, just enough to land a charged Q and deny the execute.

edits.before: Two items into late game your max-HP total via Heartsteel stacks and your kill-passive HP bonuses push your effective durability past what a single Akali rotation can delete. She needs to land both R casts plus a full Q-E-Q chain — your W-shield absorbs one burst window and your zombie passive spends 6-8 seconds as a frontline threat even if she completes the combo. Push side lanes with Unstoppable Onslaught as a transit tool, force her to match you or concede towers, and make her burn R just to disengage from a zombie. The lane is roughly even across the full game: you own the pre-6 stun threat and the very late brawl, she owns the level-6 burst window and the mid-fight untargetability — never forget she can shroud mid-trade to dodge your second charged Q.
edits.after: Two items into late game your max-HP total via Heartsteel stacks and your kill-passive HP bonuses push your effective durability past what a single Akali rotation can delete. She needs both R casts plus a full Q-E-Q chain — Soul Furnace absorbs one burst window and your zombie passive spends 6-8 seconds as a frontline threat even if she completes the combo. Push side lanes with Unstoppable Onslaught as a transit tool, force her to match you or concede towers, and make her burn R just to disengage from a zombie. You own the pre-6 stun threat and the very late brawl, she owns the level-6 burst window — and remember Twilight Shroud only hides her from your aim, so swing where she stood, not where you can see.

notes: Chart flipped to the packet shape, which the entry's own whys already described; proposed as matched pairs. The mirror's hard correction is carried over: Twilight Shroud denies aim, it does not blank a ground-area Decimating Smash. Also removed a false mechanical claim that Soul Furnace is physical damage reduction. Akali's Q cooldown was written as a 3-second window; the kit says 1.5s, Energy-gated.
